resources.string: Tune game frame rates through their config files
Only installed games are shown. Connect Shizuku to scan the Android/data folders.
Open the \"Games\" tab and tap the game you want to tune.
Can\'t reach the game folder yet. Connect Shizuku first.
The game overwrote your FPS setting. It is now %1$s instead of %2$s (this usually happens after a game update or a graphics change in-game).
Always close the game before scanning and editing
Walks every folder in Android/data/%1$s, reads small files and looks for FPS-related keys such as fps, FrameRate or FrameRateLimit.
Scan for FPS files and keys
Tap to use that file and key
Tap to select and view · showing the first %1$d
Pick from the scan results or type them in
FPS key name in the file
A running game writes its old values back when it exits. Recommended.
Add the key if it\'s missing
Only use this when you know the exact key the game reads. A wrong name is simply ignored by the game.
Games differ. Some use 0 or -1 to mean \"unlimited\".
The selected value (%1$d) is higher than the display can show (%2$dHz). It won\'t look smoother, but the phone will run hotter and drain faster.
Going above the display refresh rate doesn\'t look smoother; it only adds heat and battery drain.
A floating counter to check whether FPS really changed

Reads frame timing from the system through Shizuku. If the game\'s surface is found it measures only the game (game); otherwise it measures the whole screen (screen). Drag the counter to move it and long-press it to close.
Works with any game, even when its files can\'t be edited

Know the limit: Android has no way to push a game above the FPS cap the game sets for itself. The system can do two things: stop the display from lowering its refresh rate while you play, and hold the game\'s FPS steady (it can lower FPS, not raise it).
On · display is now %1$dHz (if it doesn\'t change, your ROM ignores this setting)
Stops the system from lowering Hz during play. Uses more battery, so turn it off when you\'re done.
On for this game · relaunch the game to apply
Sets Performance mode and caps FPS at the target above (30/40/45/60/90/120) for steadier frames and less heat. Some brands don\'t support it.
Original files saved before the first edit. Restore them any time.
The original file is backed up first (on the first edit), so you can restore it later.
Shizuku is connected and allowed. The app can read and edit files in Android/data.
Wait a moment. If it takes long, tap Check again.
Shizuku is running but this app isn\'t allowed yet
Update Shizuku to the latest version from the Play Store.
Follow the guide below step by step. It takes about 5 minutes and you only do it once.
The steps and fixes below are tailored to this brand.
Shizuku lets this app use adb-level access to reach the game\'s Android/data folder without root.
Get Shizuku (by Xingchen & Rikka) from the Play Store. It\'s free.
Settings > About device > Version > tap \"Build number\" 7 times, then enter your screen lock. Developer options are under Settings > System (or Additional settings) > Developer options.
Settings > About phone > tap \"OS version\" (HyperOS/MIUI) 7 times, then enter your screen lock. Developer options are under Settings > Additional settings > Developer options.
Settings > About phone > Software information > tap \"Build number\" 7 times, then enter your screen lock. Developer options appear at the bottom of Settings.
Settings > About phone > tap \"Build number\" 7 times, then enter your screen lock until it says you are a developer. Developer options are usually under Settings > System.

Connect to Wi-Fi first (internet isn\'t required, but you must be on Wi-Fi). In Developer options, turn on \"Wireless debugging\" and allow it when asked about this network.\n\nTip: also turn on \"Disable adb authorization timeout\" if your phone has it, so you don\'t have to pair again every few days.

1) Open Shizuku. Under "Start via Wireless debugging" tap "Pairing". Shizuku shows a persistent notification (allow notifications if asked).
2) Go back to "Wireless debugging" and tap "Pair device with pairing code". A 6-digit code appears.
3) Without closing the code screen, pull down the notification shade, tap "Enter pairing code" in Shizuku's notification and type the 6 digits.
4) Wait until the notification says pairing succeeded.

In Shizuku, tap \"Start\" in the same section and wait until the home screen says Shizuku is running.\n\nAfter every reboot, turn Wireless debugging back on and tap \"Start\" again. You don\'t need to pair again.
Come back to FPS Unlocker, tap \"Allow Shizuku\" in the card above and choose \"Allow all the time\". The status at the top right turns green.
This brand often limits adb permissions. If step 6 says \"the permission of adb is limited\", see the highlighted fix under Common problems below.
Shizuku says \"the permission of adb is limited\"
ColorOS 16 and newer: open Developer options and turn on \"Disable system optimization\". Confirm the warning.
If you can\'t find it, switch the phone language to English for a moment (Settings > System > Language). Some languages hide this option. Switch back afterwards.
ColorOS older than 16: use \"Disable permission monitoring\" instead.
Then open Shizuku, tap \"Stop\" and \"Start\" again. If it still fails, reboot once and start Shizuku again.
Open Developer options and turn on \"USB debugging (Security settings)\". It\'s a different switch from the normal USB debugging.
Xiaomi may require a SIM card and a signed-in Mi Account before this switch can be turned on.
Open Developer options and turn off \"Flyme payment protection\".
Shizuku won\'t start or adb won\'t connect
If \"Auto Blocker\" is on, it can block adb. Turn it off for now in Settings > Security and privacy > Auto Blocker.
Then pair and start Shizuku again using the steps above.
The pairing code field doesn\'t appear in the notification
Allow Shizuku\'s notifications in Settings > Apps > Shizuku > Notifications.
If it still doesn\'t show, use split screen: Shizuku on one half and the Wireless debugging screen on the other.
Pairing codes expire quickly. If it fails, close the code screen and get a new code.
Shizuku stops after a reboot or a Wi-Fi change
This is normal when Shizuku is started through Wireless debugging: the system turns Wireless debugging off after a reboot or when Wi-Fi drops.
Connect to Wi-Fi, turn Wireless debugging back on, then tap \"Start\" in Shizuku. No need to pair again.
Scan finds no config file, or only encrypted ones
Most games (Unity games, for example) keep their settings in /data/data/<package>, not Android/data. Shizuku started through Wireless debugging (adb level) can\'t open that folder.
If your phone is rooted (Magisk / KernelSU), start Shizuku with root. The app then also scans /data/data, shown as a folder named internal, and the game card gets a root badge.
If the files are encrypted, the app will not try to decrypt them. Use \"System-level FPS control\" instead and check the result with the FPS meter.
The app says Shizuku is off even though it\'s running
Check that Shizuku\'s home screen really says it\'s running.
Tap \"Check again\" here, or swipe this app away and reopen it.
If you tapped \"Deny\" before, open Shizuku > Authorized applications and turn on FPS Unlocker.
Grants access to the selected game\'s folder only, without Shizuku
Choose a game in the \"Games\" tab first
Grant access to the game folder
On the screen that opens, tap \"Use this folder\" and then \"Allow\".

Editing files of online games may break the game\'s terms of service, and anti-cheat systems may detect it. Try a secondary account first. This app can only edit plain-text files. If a game encrypts its settings or sets FPS from its servers, the app can\'t change it and will not try to break the encryption.
Unknown engine, possibly the publisher\'s in-house engine. Scan to see whether its files are readable text.
Unreal games often keep settings in …/Saved/Config/Android/*.ini as plain text, so there\'s a good chance it can be edited.
Unity games usually keep settings in PlayerPrefs under /data/data, which needs root. Some games also write their own settings files to Android/data.
Scan to see whether the game stores its settings as text files.
Drag the counter to move it · long-press it to close
Key \"%1$s\" not found in the file (check upper/lower case, or Scan to see the real keys)
No { } in this JSON file, can\'t add a key
Not a SharedPreferences file (no </map>), can\'t add a key
Can\'t open the granted folder. Request access again.
" · /data/data of the game was not scanned (needs Shizuku started with root)"
Found %1$d keys that look FPS-related. Tap one to select it, then view the file before tapping Apply.
No FPS-named key found, but there are %1$d text files. Try opening files whose names contain config, setting or prefs.%2$s
All files are binary or encrypted%1$s. The app can\'t edit files like these; try \"System-level FPS control\" instead.%2$s
No files found in the game folder. The game may keep its settings in /data/data.%1$s
Small files %1$d%2$s · text %3$d · binary/encrypted %4$d · FPS keys %5$d
Enter a value for Max first
This file is binary or encrypted; the app can\'t edit it
The file already has %1$s, nothing to change
Prepared %1$d changed lines, waiting for confirmation
The file changed while waiting for confirmation (the game may be running). Close the game and tap Apply again.
Set %1$s = %2$s%3$s · %4$s · open the game and check with the FPS meter
Backup file is gone (it may have been deleted with the game data)
Display locked at %1$sHz (some brands ignore this; check the current Hz in the card)
Game Mode set to Performance with FPS capped at %1$d. Relaunch the game to apply.
Game Mode for this game turned off
Display over other apps isn\'t allowed yet
FPS meter started. Open your game now (long-press the counter to close it).
%1$s: can\'t reach the game folder yet (choose a game and connect Shizuku first)
